_note: WAVE-50 LANE B1 — the full-corpus re-extract + re-convert differential for the declaration-validity oracle added to tools/titan/extract-fixture.mjs (docs/BACKLOG.md ranked item 0(a); the wave-49 patch was lost with its session scratchpad and was re-derived here). THE RESULT IN ONE LINE: across all 1435 gate-corpus tests, re-extracted and re-converted on both sides of the change, exactly ONE fixture, ONE per-test-IR document and ONE component differ — css-values/angle-units-001, whose 100x100 div regains the `background-image: linear-gradient(green, green)` that four INVALID later declarations had deleted. Zero unintended byte changes. The change is NOT device-measured: wave 50 ran no gate, so the three predicted cell flips below are predictions with numbers, adjudicated from the frozen wave49-final captures and the frozen browser ref, not from a run.

defect.seam: tools/titan/extract-fixture.mjs — the per-rule declaration collapse was a bare `props[k] = v` (last-wins, no validity oracle), plus the same bare last-wins at the cross-rule merges in propsForElement / propsForBodyRoot and in the style="" bag.
defect.why: css-syntax-3 §2.2 (Error Handling): a declaration whose value does not match the property's grammar is ignored, LEAVING THE PREVIOUSLY DECLARED VALUE IN FORCE. The converter implements exactly that (converter/src/main/kotlin/app/parsing/css/properties/PropertiesParser.kt — `Dropped invalid declaration … (css-syntax-3 §2.2)`, InvalidDeclaration sentinel), but never got the chance: the extractor had already deleted the earlier valid declaration.
defect.carrier: wave49-final css-values/angle-units-001 web f 0.9990 · ios f 0.9974 · android f 0.9966 (all three cF, novelInkFailed true)

fix.oracle: provablyInvalidDeclaration(prop, value) — CONSERVATIVE: returns a reason only for a value invalid in EVERY CSS context, null otherwise. One rule today (R1): a <dimension-token> whose unit is outside the closed CSS unit tables (css-values-4 §6.1.1 / §6.1.2 / §6.2 / §7.1 / §7.2 / §7.3 / §7.4, css-grid-2 §7.2.3 <flex>, css-contain-3 container-relative lengths).
fix.guard: assignDeclaration(target, key, value) refuses an incoming value ONLY when it is provably invalid AND the value it would overwrite is not. Invalid-over-invalid still ends on the last member (byte-identical to the historical path). A refused declaration contributes neither its value nor its `!important` flag.
fix.breadcrumb: Every refusal is pushed onto `invalidShadowDrops` and printed on that test's extract.log line as `[validity: N shadowing declaration(s) refused — <prop>: kept '<v>', dropped '<v>' (<reason>)]`. No silent fallthrough.
notCovered: The LAYERED cascade path (resolveLayeredCascade, css-cascade-5 §6.4.4 + revert-layer) keeps the unguarded sort: zero corpus carriers, and a candidate filter inside that sort could only risk the css-cascade cells. Stated in the code.

The OLDER importance defect of the same collapse (`a: x !important; a: y` still ends on `y`, where §6.4.4 says the important declaration wins). Zero corpus carriers — see duplicate-declaration-census.json for the population.

method.isolation: tools/titan/extract-fixture.mjs is being edited by more than one wave-50 lane at once (lane B4's omitted-end-tag work landed in the same file mid-run). The differential therefore does NOT diff the working tree: it diffs HEAD (747b28e4) against HEAD + ONLY this lane's hunks, each copied into its own runner directory under the session scratchpad, so no other lane's in-flight edit can enter either side.
method.extract: 1435 tests (the union of the 30 wave49-final tests.list files), WPT_FIXTURES_ROOT redirected per side; static path only (POST_LOAD_EXTRACT / BIDI_BAKE / VT_BAKE off on BOTH sides) — the host had ~56 MB free and BACKLOG's quiet-host rule says defer browser work rather than retry it.
method.convert: build-combined-fixture.mjs per section on each side, then the converter run from ONE fixed build (converter/build/classes/kotlin/main, built 2026-09-05 22:13) used for both sides, then split-combined-ir.mjs per section.
method.bakeArgument: The static-only run is complete for the baked pipeline too: the oracle fires on exactly 4 declarations in the whole corpus, all in angle-units-001, and that test engaged NO bake in wave49-final (its extract.log line carries no post-load / bidi / counter / vt note). Independently confirmed: this lane's BASE per-test-IR for angle-units-001 is byte-identical to wave49-final's.
method.residualRisk: The 29 unchanged sections were re-converted with a 2026-09-05 converter build, so a corpus-wide base-vs-wave49-final IR comparison is not apples-to-apples (615 of 1435 documents differ from wave49-final, from the retro's 109-file converter change plus the absent bakes). That comparison is NOT part of this differential; the differential is mine-vs-base with the converter held fixed.

capabilityEvidence: angle-units-002/003/004/005 are the SAME document with a valid winning declaration (`linear-gradient(90DeG, green, green)`) and already pass on all three at web 0.9990 / ios 0.9974 / android 0.9967 — the same SSIMs 001 fails at. The stacking (position:relative, bottom:100px, z-index:-1), the geometry and the gradient rendering are therefore already correct on all three; 001 differed only in that its winner was invalid.

A bare 2-stop null-position linear-gradient renders on all three today: css-break/background-image-004/005/006 and css-images/gradient-button pass on all three, and their captures carry the declared gradient colours (rgb(0,128,0) / rgb(255,0,0) / blue-green ramps).
